findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass` body. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class retains a non-empty `__abstractmethods__` and `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` unconditionally, so any `Detector` row with `type="metric_alert_fire"` fed to `process_detectors` will now crash instead of returning no results as it did before this change (the previous implementation had a concrete no-op `evaluate`). Either implement the abstract members (even as stubs that raise `NotImplementedError` with a clear message) or keep a concrete handler until the metric-alert detector is actually built. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` comment on line 10 is also now stale.

findings.title: Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe is built for the wrong group key
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected `IssueOccurrence` is produced via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with `expected_result.group_key == "group_key"`. The handler's `build_occurrence_and_event_data` therefore calls `build_fingerprint("group_key")` producing `["<id>:group_key"]`, while the expected occurrence has fingerprint `["<id>:val1"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a dataclass whose generated `__eq__` compares `fingerprint`, so `expected_result` cannot equal the actual `DetectorEvaluationResult` and the assertion on line 546-560 should fail (if it somehow passes, the comparison is not actually verifying the occurrence contents). The expected occurrence should be built with the same group key (`"group_key"`) and value (`10`) that are passed to `evaluate_group_key_value`.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still describes a list return value
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed in this PR to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`" and "There will be one result for each group key". The docstring should be updated to say it returns a dict keyed by group key, so implementers of other handlers aren't misled about the contract (which `process_detectors` now relies on via `.values()`).
